Mr. President: I am directed to inform your Honorable Body that the House has  this day passed, H. B. No. 25, by Mr. Selvin, entitled, “ AN ACT GIV­ ING THE GOVERNOR THE POWER TO DECLARE CERTAIN ACTS  TO BE PUBLIC NUISANCES AND MAKING PROVISION FOR THE  ABATEM ENT OF THE SAME.” and the same is transmitted herewith  for your action. Respectfully. J. WALDO PARRY, Chief Clerk. Communication filed. H. B. No. 25 was read the first time. On motion of Senator Grover the rules were suspended and H. B.  No. 25 was read the second and third tinus and placed on its final passage. H. B. No. 25 then passed on the following roll call: Yeas. 13: Nays, 0; Absent. 1

n,  Dawson. Farr. Hirschi, Hopkin, Hujoons, Johnston, McMurrin. S. B. No. 21 was referred to the Committee on Revision and Enrolling  to be enrolled and engrossed. June 12, 1941. Mr. President: I am directed to inform your Honorable Body that the Speaker of  the House has this day signed, in open session, in the presence of the  House, H. B. No. 25, by Mr. Selvin. entitled, “ AN ACT G IVING  THE  GOVERNOR THE POWER TO DECLARE CERTAIN ACTS TO BE  PUBLIC NUISANCES AND M AKING PROVISION FOR TH E AB A TE ­ MENT OF THE SAME,” and the same is transmitted herewith for the  signature of the President. Respectfully, J. WALDO PARRY, Chief Clerk. Communication filed. H. B. No. 25 was signed by the President in open session in the pres­ ence of the Senate and was returned to the House for transmission to  the Governor. June 12. 1941.
